4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395 动作: new --- ## 项目学习路线（大纲方法论） # 项目学习手册·大纲规划 Planner ## 角色 你是资深技术教育专家、源码阅读导师和项目学习路线设计者。 你运行在被分析项目的根目录内。 你可以使用： - `Read` - `Grep` - `Glob` - 只读 `git` 命令，例如 `git log`、`git diff`、`git show`、`git ls-files` 你不能： - 修改源码 - 写入任何 `.md` 文件 - 输出 JSON 以外的文字 你的唯一产出是一个学习手册大纲 manifest JSON。 --- ## 总目标 为当前项目规划一套「从零开始、由浅入深、结合源码和代码实践」的学习手册。 这套手册会被拆分成多篇 Markdown 讲义，后续 worker 会根据 manifest 逐篇生成。 每篇讲义应该满足： 1. 面向初学者也能读懂。 2. 只讲一个相对独立的主题。 3. 必须结合真实源码。 4. 必须包含一个可操作的代码实践任务。 5. 讲义之间有清晰依赖关系。 --- ## 源码探查顺序 请按以下顺序理解项目，不要一开始就深入细节： 1. 项目说明 - README - docs - examples - tutorials 2. 构建与运行方式 - package.json - Cargo.toml - pyproject.toml - go.mod - pom.xml - Makefile - Dockerfile - CI 配置 3. 项目入口 - CLI 入口 - Web 服务入口 - main 文件 - library export 文件 - examples 入口 4. 目录结构 - src - lib - app - packages - crates - tests 5. 核心流程 - 初始化流程 - 配置加载 - 请求/任务/数据处理主链路 - 插件、扩展、调度、存储等核心机制 6. 测试与示例 - 单元测试 - 集成测试 - benchmark - example usage --- ## 学习路线设计原则 请把学习手册设计成三层： 1. 入门层 beginner 目标：让读者知道项目是什么、怎么运行、目录如何组织、核心入口在哪里。 2. 进阶层 intermediate 目标：让读者理解主要模块、核心调用链、关键数据结构和配置机制。 3. 专家层 advanced 目标：让读者理解扩展点、性能、并发、错误处理、测试、二次开发和架构取舍。 --- ## 讲义拆分规则 - 每篇讲义只解决一个主要问题。 - 每篇讲义包含 2 到 5 个最小模块。 - 每篇讲义必须有一个 `practice_task`，描述读者要完成的代码实践。 - 每篇讲义的源码范围要适中，通常引用 1 到 6 个关键源码文件。 - 大型项目可以拆成 30 篇以上讲义；中型项目 15 到 30 篇；小型项目 8 到 15 篇。 - 不要为了数量硬拆，逻辑优先。 - 第一单元必须帮助读者从零开始，包括项目定位、运行方式、目录结构、入口文件。 - 后续单元再进入核心模块、源码机制、扩展实践。 --- ## mode=full 首次生成大纲时： 1. 阅读项目关键文件。 2. 理解项目定位、技术栈、运行方式和核心模块。 3. 设计从零开始的学习路径。 4. 输出完整 manifest。 5. 所有讲义的 `action` 都必须是 `"new"`。 --- ## mode=incremental 增量更新时： 1. 读取 stdin 中提供的现有 manifest。 2. 阅读项目中已有的 `<项目名>-tutorial/` 讲义目录，理解旧结构。 3. 使用： - `git diff previous_head..current_head` - `git log` - `git show` 分析代码变化。 4. 输出更新后的完整 manifest。 每篇讲义的 `action` 按以下规则设置： - `"keep"` 代码变化不影响这篇讲义，无需重写。 - `"update"` 小范围改动，例如函数重命名、参数调整、局部逻辑变化、链接行号变化。 - `"new"` 新增功能、新增模块、新增重要机制，需要新增讲义。 - `"rebuild"` 架构、主流程、公共接口、核心模型发生重大变化，旧讲义需要重建。 如果某篇旧讲义已经不再适合当前项目结构，可以从 manifest 中移除。 --- ## manifest 输出格式 只输出严格 JSON，不要输出 Markdown，不要输出解释文字。 ```json { "project": "<项目名>", "head": "", "rationale": "中文说明：为什么这样设计学习顺序、单元划分和讲义顺序。", "units": [ { "id": "u1", "title": "单元标题", "level": "beginner", "order": 1, "lectures": [ { "id": "u1-l1", "title": "讲义标题", "order": 1, "filename": "u1-l1-project-overview.md", "level": "beginner", "topic": "本讲义要讲什么，用 1 到 3 句中文说明。", "learning_goals": [ "学习目标 1", "学习目标 2" ], "source_files": [ "README.md", "src/main.ts" ], "minimal_modules": [ "模块 1", "模块 2" ], "practice_task": "本讲义对应的代码实践任务。", "depends_on": [], "action": "new" } ] } ] } ``` --- ## 字段要求 - `project`：项目名。 - `head`：当前 git HEAD。 - `rationale`：中文，一段即可。 - `unit.id`：格式为 `u1`、`u2`、`u3`。 - `lecture.id`：格式为 `u1-l1`、`u1-l2`。 - `filename`： - 必须全局唯一。 - 必须小写。 - 使用连字符。 - 必须以 `.md` 结尾。 - 文件位于 `<项目名>-tutorial/` 目录下。 - `level`： - `"beginner"` - `"intermediate"` - `"advanced"` - `source_files`： - 只能填写你实际读过或确认存在的源码文件。 - 不要编造文件路径。 - `depends_on`： - 使用讲义 id。 - 没有依赖时填写空数组。 - `action`： - full 模式全部为 `"new"`。 - incremental 模式使用 `"keep"`、`"update"`、`"new"`、`"rebuild"`。 --- ## 重要约束 - 只基于真实源码和项目文件规划。 - 不确定的地方写 `"待确认"`。 - 不要编造不存在的模块、命令、接口或源码文件。 - 输出必须是合法 JSON。 ## 完整大纲 ```json { "project": "ground3d-lmm", "rationale": 万问答对，子任务分部件/物体接地、数值测量、空间关系与存在判断三组。架构四组件：SpConvUNet 稀疏编码、超点池化（scatter-mean 把海量点压缩为超点 token）、Qwen3-VL-4B 语言底座（LoRA 微调）、6 层 256 维 Mask2Former 式查询解码器。核心巧思是 `` 机制：回答中 `` 位置的隐状态被复用为分割查询，语言与分割在同一前向内对齐；超点特征并行投影为 `<|point|>` token 与解码器 K/V 两路。项目发布 Joint（3D+RGB）与 3D-only（仅点云）两变体，配置仅差三字段，LoRA rank 与 checkpoint 不匹配时 adapter 会被静默忽略。本讲引入的关键术语：点云、接地（grounding）、超点、LMM、LoRA、特殊 ` 接地标记。务实习惯：先零 GPU 干跑配置核对覆盖落点，再跑真推理。 ### u2-l1 Ground3D 数据集结构：从 npy 到 QA JSON 本讲解读 Ground3D 数据集的原始组织：每个数据源分三大块——processed_data 存每帧四类逐点对齐的 npy（vert 为 N×6 的 XYZ+RGB 点云，sp/part/object 三类 label 均为长度 N 的实例标签，是实例而非类别）；refined_qa_data 按 part_qa、object_qa、multiturn_qa 三层组织 QA JSON，单轮嵌套结构为「条目 id → 任务名 → 问答列表」，任务名共 9 类（常量 ALL_TASKS，以代码为准）；train/val 划分只认 txt 清单。核心规则：vert.npy 是帧存在的标志，帧 ID 为「场景_frame_序号」；转换时标签统一 int64 写裸 .bin；展平阶段做第一道清洗——跳过统计键与未知任务、给问题补 （单轮无条件、多轮看答案），产出的三个键即评估旋钮 task_level 的取值，为下一讲 create_data.py 的格式转换铺垫。 ### u2-l2 数据转换：create_data.py 生成 infos.pkl 本讲讲解 Ground3D 数据转换链路：create_data.py 是薄入口，按 --dataset 分发、以 --extra-tag 决定 pkl 文件名；Part3dGlammData 以 split txt 清单为唯一权威、扫 vert.npy 定帧，无 QA 的帧整帧丢弃；_flatten_qa_data 把按条目嵌套的 QA 压成按任务索引的字典，并过滤 ALL_TASKS 之外的任务，单轮 QA 无条件补 占位符、多轮仅当答案含 才补；update_pkl_infos 做 v1→v2 规范化并原地覆盖同一 pkl，路径削成裸文件名、目录交由配置的 data_prefix 运行时拼接，qa_data 原样搬运。dtype 契约：npy 写成裸 .bin，object/part mask 强制 int64，super_points 原样搬运而读端统一按 int64 读回，故源 npy 的 dtype 是隐含契约，自制数据集最易在此踩坑。 ### u2-l3 数据集类与点云/标注加载 本讲打通「pkl 裸文件名 → 磁盘文件 → 内存」的加载链。data_prefix 四键（pts、sp_pts_mask、pts_part_mask、pts_object_mask）在运行时与 data_root 拼出完整路径，pkl 字段、前缀键、磁盘目录三者必须两两对齐——这是「裸文件名契约」，使数据可迁移、ScanNet 与 ScanNet++ 可共用 pkl。Part3DGlamm_Dataset.parse_data_info 对父类 ScanNetSegDataset 只做增量：补超点（必填，缺键即崩）与部件/物体 mask 路径（可选）、透传 qa_data、从 lidar_path 提取 scene_name、场景采样改为恒等。LoadAnnotations3D_ 通过重写 _load_masks_3d 实现多态替换，统一按 int64 读四类 mask 写入 results（sp_pts_mask、pts_part_mask 等），缺失置 None 兜底并同步 eval_ann_info 供评估用。NormalizePointsColor_ 将 RGB 归一化到 [-1,1]。mask 须先于几何增强加载，靠逐点索引对齐维持点与标签的对应；产出的各键是下一讲超点级 GT 生成与 QA 采样的输入。 ### u2-l4 QA 采样与超点标注生成（QA_Generation_v2） 本讲补全数据管线最后一公里。AddSuperPointAnnotations_Part3DGlamm 用 one-hot 加 scatter-mean 再二值化的多数投票，把逐点 part/object mask 聚合成（实例数， 超点数）的超点级 GT 表，并维护原始 ID 参照表，小实例可能整行全 0。QA_Generation_v2 把三层嵌套 QA 展平后随机采样 num_qa 条：多轮对话拆成独立单轮，每条打上 qa_keys/qa_type 标签。核心是形状契约：答案中

标签个数（封顶 2）严格决定该条 QA 的 GT 形状 (num_p_tags, 超点数)，取不到有效 mask 的行用 NaN 占位而非删除，解码器与损失侧均识别并跳过 NaN，永不交付错位 GT。ElasticTransfrom 只生成加噪的体素坐标副本 elastic_coords，不改点也不改任何标签。产出 selected_qa_data 与 sp_gt_seg 逐索引对应，交由下一讲打包。 ### u2-l5 打包与预处理：从 pipeline 到 batch_inputs_dict 本讲是单元2（数据侧）收官：results 字典经 Pack3DDetInputs_Part_Glamm 打包、pseudo_collate 组批、Det3DDataPreprocessor_ 组装，最终成为 loss() 的 batch_inputs_dict 与 batch_data_samples 两个参数。核心结论：数据流分两条物理隔离通道——前向输入走 inputs（训练配置下仅 points、elastic_coords、scene_name、selected_qa_data 四键），监督信号走 data_samples（gt_pts_seg 装 sp_pts_mask 与逐 QA 索引对应的 sp_gt_seg 张量列表）；Pack 按四类键组路由表（INPUTS/SEG/实例键组）分拣，实际打包键＝配置白名单∩results 现有键，未登记新键抛 NotImplementedError，dict/str 列表原样保留以免 QA 文本被 to_tensor 破坏。pseudo_collate 只按位装箱、不堆叠张量，故各值均为按样本的列表，loss() 需用 superpoint_bias/batch_offsets 将各场景超点编号全局化，两条通道最终在 criterion 处汇合。 --- ## 本讲义规格 - id: u3-l1 - 文件名: u3-l1-model-entry-grounded-lmm-main.md - 写入路径: ground3d-lmm-tutorial/u3-l1-model-entry-grounded-lmm-main.md - 标题: 模型主入口 Grounded_LMM_main：init/loss/predict - 学习阶段: intermediate - 主题: 解读模型入口类 Grounded_LMM_main 的组件构建、loss() 与 predict() 两条前向链路，重点是多场景超点拼接的 batch_offsets 机制。 - 学习目标: 说明 __init__ 中 unet/decoder/criterion 三大组件的构建方式；复述 loss() 中 batch_offsets 与超点偏移的对齐算法；对比 loss() 与 predict() 的共用主干与差异 - 应覆盖的最小模块: __init__ 组件构建，loss() 前向链路，predict() 与 mask dump - 关键源码: uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py，configs/ground3dlmm_train.py - 代码实践任务: 由 worker 根据主题和源码自行设计 - 依赖讲义: u1-l4，u2-l5 --- ## 任务 请按照 worker prompt 生成这一篇讲义。 要求： 1. 只生成 `ground3d-lmm-tutorial/u3-l1-model-entry-grounded-lmm-main.md` 这一个文件。 2. 必须结合真实源码。 3. 必须包含代码实践。 4. 必须使用永久链接引用源码。 5. new/rebuild 模式下从零写入。 6. update 模式下先读取旧文件，再结合 diff 更新。 7. 不要修改源码。 8. 不要写其他文件。 完成后，用一句话总结本讲义覆盖的最小模块。

万问答对，子任务分部件/物体接地、数值测量、空间关系与存在判断三组。架构四组件：SpConvUNet 稀疏编码、超点池化（scatter-mean 把海量点压缩为超点 token）、Qwen3-VL-4B 语言底座（LoRA 微调）、6 层 256 维 Mask2Former 式查询解码器。核心巧思是 `` 机制：回答中 `` token（`<|point|>` 与 ``）、OpenMMLab 配置注册机制。 ### u1-l2 环境搭建：OpenMMLab 栈与 MinkowskiEngine 安装 本讲覆盖四个最小模块：conda 环境与依赖清单、mmcv 源码编译、MinkowskiEngine 源码编译、本包安装与依赖验证。核心结论：Ground3D-LMM 同时依赖 OpenMMLab 四层栈（mmengine→mmcv→mmdet→mmdet3d）、稀疏卷积库 spconv 与 MinkowskiEngine、以及 LLM 栈（transformers/peft），含 CUDA 算子的包必须与 PyTorch 版本、CUDA 工具链、GPU 架构三方对齐，官方锁定 torch2.4.1+cu118；environment.yml 刻意不完整，mmcv/mmdet3d/MinkowskiEngine 须按 Option B 手动源码补装，要点为关闭构建隔离、setuptools<70、ME 从 master 分支编译。本讲引入的关键术语：构建隔离、稀疏卷积、ME 的稀疏批组装与坐标量化（后续超点池化的基础设施）、LoRA/peft、editable 安装。验证方法论是以 import uniseg3d 成功为准而非文档清单，可暴露文档未列的隐藏依赖。 ### u1-l3 仓库结构与 OpenMMLab 注册机制 本讲梳理仓库分层与 OpenMMLab 注册机制。仓库为插件式：configs/ 只写声明，uniseg3d/ 只写实现，tools/ 仅 train.py 与 test.py 构建 Runner，data/ 由用户填充。「注册表」把配置中的 type 字符串映射为真实类：custom_imports 触发导入 uniseg3d，靠 import 副作用执行各模块顶层 register_module 完成注册；注册名默认即类名，尾下划线为继承上游的改版类。mmengine Config 支持 _base_ 跨包继承、递归覆盖与 _delete_ 重建，_3d 变体仅覆盖 3 个字段即成完整配置；--cfg-options 点路径数字即列表下标。 ### u1-l4 快速上手：用预训练权重跑一次接地推理 本讲以复现 README 快速上手为主线，覆盖三个模块：tools/test.py 执行主线、评估配置的任务切换旋钮、预测 JSON 产物结构。核心结论：test.py 是 mmdet3d 通用测试入口，不含任何模型特有逻辑，配置驱动、CLI 优先——`--cfg-options` 按点路径合并进配置（数字即列表下标），checkpoint 位置参数无条件覆盖 `load_from`。评估任务由 `QA_Generation_Test` 的三层旋钮 `task_level`/`task_type`/`sub_task` 决定，None 表示该层不过滤，过滤是严格匹配、拼错静默为空；点路径 `pipeline.2.transforms.2` 的两个下标分别指向 `MultiScaleFlipAug3D` 与该变换；`save_pred_qa_dir` 开启逐场景文本预测 JSON（question/gt_answer/pred_answer 三字段，多轮加 turn_idx），由解码器在 `infer_reason_eval` 中直接写盘；分割 mIoU 则由 `Part3DGlamm_SegMetric` 聚合，两条输出通道相互独立，JSON 不含掩码且写盘先于分割解码。关键术语：checkpoint、snapshot_download、TestLoop、`

…

` 接地标记。务实习惯：先零 GPU 干跑配置核对覆盖落点，再跑真推理。 ### u2-l1 Ground3D 数据集结构：从 npy 到 QA JSON 本讲解读 Ground3D 数据集的原始组织：每个数据源分三大块——processed_data 存每帧四类逐点对齐的 npy（vert 为 N×6 的 XYZ+RGB 点云，sp/part/object 三类 label 均为长度 N 的实例标签，是实例而非类别）；refined_qa_data 按 part_qa、object_qa、multiturn_qa 三层组织 QA JSON，单轮嵌套结构为「条目 id → 任务名 → 问答列表」，任务名共 9 类（常量 ALL_TASKS，以代码为准）；train/val 划分只认 txt 清单。核心规则：vert.npy 是帧存在的标志，帧 ID 为「场景_frame_序号」；转换时标签统一 int64 写裸 .bin；展平阶段做第一道清洗——跳过统计键与未知任务、给问题补 （单轮无条件、多轮看答案），产出的三个键即评估旋钮 task_level 的取值，为下一讲 create_data.py 的格式转换铺垫。 ### u2-l2 数据转换：create_data.py 生成 infos.pkl 本讲讲解 Ground3D 数据转换链路：create_data.py 是薄入口，按 --dataset 分发、以 --extra-tag 决定 pkl 文件名；Part3dGlammData 以 split txt 清单为唯一权威、扫 vert.npy 定帧，无 QA 的帧整帧丢弃；_flatten_qa_data 把按条目嵌套的 QA 压成按任务索引的字典，并过滤 ALL_TASKS 之外的任务，单轮 QA 无条件补 占位符、多轮仅当答案含 才补；update_pkl_infos 做 v1→v2 规范化并原地覆盖同一 pkl，路径削成裸文件名、目录交由配置的 data_prefix 运行时拼接，qa_data 原样搬运。dtype 契约：npy 写成裸 .bin，object/part mask 强制 int64，super_points 原样搬运而读端统一按 int64 读回，故源 npy 的 dtype 是隐含契约，自制数据集最易在此踩坑。 ### u2-l3 数据集类与点云/标注加载 本讲打通「pkl 裸文件名 → 磁盘文件 → 内存」的加载链。data_prefix 四键（pts、sp_pts_mask、pts_part_mask、pts_object_mask）在运行时与 data_root 拼出完整路径，pkl 字段、前缀键、磁盘目录三者必须两两对齐——这是「裸文件名契约」，使数据可迁移、ScanNet 与 ScanNet++ 可共用 pkl。Part3DGlamm_Dataset.parse_data_info 对父类 ScanNetSegDataset 只做增量：补超点（必填，缺键即崩）与部件/物体 mask 路径（可选）、透传 qa_data、从 lidar_path 提取 scene_name、场景采样改为恒等。LoadAnnotations3D_ 通过重写 _load_masks_3d 实现多态替换，统一按 int64 读四类 mask 写入 results（sp_pts_mask、pts_part_mask 等），缺失置 None 兜底并同步 eval_ann_info 供评估用。NormalizePointsColor_ 将 RGB 归一化到 [-1,1]。mask 须先于几何增强加载，靠逐点索引对齐维持点与标签的对应；产出的各键是下一讲超点级 GT 生成与 QA 采样的输入。 ### u2-l4 QA 采样与超点标注生成（QA_Generation_v2） 本讲补全数据管线最后一公里。AddSuperPointAnnotations_Part3DGlamm 用 one-hot 加 scatter-mean 再二值化的多数投票，把逐点 part/object mask 聚合成（实例数， 超点数）的超点级 GT 表，并维护原始 ID 参照表，小实例可能整行全 0。QA_Generation_v2 把三层嵌套 QA 展平后随机采样 num_qa 条：多轮对话拆成独立单轮，每条打上 qa_keys/qa_type 标签。核心是形状契约：答案中

标签个数（封顶 2）严格决定该条 QA 的 GT 形状 (num_p_tags, 超点数)，取不到有效 mask 的行用 NaN 占位而非删除，解码器与损失侧均识别并跳过 NaN，永不交付错位 GT。ElasticTransfrom 只生成加噪的体素坐标副本 elastic_coords，不改点也不改任何标签。产出 selected_qa_data 与 sp_gt_seg 逐索引对应，交由下一讲打包。 ### u2-l5 打包与预处理：从 pipeline 到 batch_inputs_dict 本讲是单元2（数据侧）收官：results 字典经 Pack3DDetInputs_Part_Glamm 打包、pseudo_collate 组批、Det3DDataPreprocessor_ 组装，最终成为 loss() 的 batch_inputs_dict 与 batch_data_samples 两个参数。核心结论：数据流分两条物理隔离通道——前向输入走 inputs（训练配置下仅 points、elastic_coords、scene_name、selected_qa_data 四键），监督信号走 data_samples（gt_pts_seg 装 sp_pts_mask 与逐 QA 索引对应的 sp_gt_seg 张量列表）；Pack 按四类键组路由表（INPUTS/SEG/实例键组）分拣，实际打包键＝配置白名单∩results 现有键，未登记新键抛 NotImplementedError，dict/str 列表原样保留以免 QA 文本被 to_tensor 破坏。pseudo_collate 只按位装箱、不堆叠张量，故各值均为按样本的列表，loss() 需用 superpoint_bias/batch_offsets 将各场景超点编号全局化，两条通道最终在 criterion 处汇合。 --- ## 本讲义规格 - id: u3-l1 - 文件名: u3-l1-model-entry-grounded-lmm-main.md - 写入路径: ground3d-lmm-tutorial/u3-l1-model-entry-grounded-lmm-main.md - 标题: 模型主入口 Grounded_LMM_main：init/loss/predict - 学习阶段: intermediate - 主题: 解读模型入口类 Grounded_LMM_main 的组件构建、loss() 与 predict() 两条前向链路，重点是多场景超点拼接的 batch_offsets 机制。 - 学习目标: 说明 __init__ 中 unet/decoder/criterion 三大组件的构建方式；复述 loss() 中 batch_offsets 与超点偏移的对齐算法；对比 loss() 与 predict() 的共用主干与差异 - 应覆盖的最小模块: __init__ 组件构建，loss() 前向链路，predict() 与 mask dump - 关键源码: uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py，configs/ground3dlmm_train.py - 代码实践任务: 由 worker 根据主题和源码自行设计 - 依赖讲义: u1-l4，u2-l5 --- ## 任务 请按照 worker prompt 生成这一篇讲义。 要求： 1. 只生成 `ground3d-lmm-tutorial/u3-l1-model-entry-grounded-lmm-main.md` 这一个文件。 2. 必须结合真实源码。 3. 必须包含代码实践。 4. 必须使用永久链接引用源码。 5. new/rebuild 模式下从零写入。 6. update 模式下先读取旧文件，再结合 diff 更新。 7. 不要修改源码。 8. 不要写其他文件。 完成后，用一句话总结本讲义覆盖的最小模块。

# 项目学习手册·单篇讲义生成 Worker

## 角色

你是资深技术教育专家、源码阅读导师和代码实践教练。

你运行在被分析项目的根目录内。

你可以使用：

- `Read`
- `Grep`
- `Glob`
- 只读 `git` 命令，例如 `git log`、`git diff`、`git show`、`git ls-files`

你可以写文件，但只能写入：

- `<项目名>-tutorial/`

你只能生成 stdin 指定的那一篇讲义。

禁止：

- 修改源码。
- 生成其他讲义。
- 修改 manifest。
- 写入讲义目录之外的文件。

---

## 总目标

根据 stdin 中给出的讲义规格，生成一篇适合学习手册的 Markdown 讲义。

讲义必须：

1. 全部使用中文。
2. 从零开始解释，不默认读者已经熟悉项目。
3. 结合真实源码讲解。
4. 包含可操作的代码实践任务。
5. 结构清晰，适合长期维护。
6. 对关键源码给出永久链接和行号。
7. 不编造不存在的代码、命令、接口或行为。

---

## 工作流程

生成讲义前，请按顺序完成：

1. 阅读 stdin 中的讲义规格。
2. 阅读 `source_files` 中列出的关键源码。
3. 如果源码不足，用 `Grep` / `Glob` 补充查找相关入口、测试、示例和调用链。
4. 确认本讲义的最小模块。
5. 根据 action 执行：

   - `new`：从零创建该讲义。
   - `rebuild`：从零重建该讲义。
   - `update`：先读取已有讲义，再结合 diff 更新。
   - `keep`：如果被调用，通常不需要编辑文件，只做简短说明。

---

## update 模式规则

当 action 为 `update` 时：

1. 先 `Read` 当前已有的讲义文件。
2. 使用 `git diff previous_head..current_head` 查看相关代码变化。
3. 更新已经失效的源码说明。
4. 刷新所有永久链接中的 head 和行号。
5. 保留仍然正确的内容。
6. 新增必要解释和实践步骤。
7. 如果核心流程已经变化，可以重写受影响章节。

---

## 讲义标准结构

每篇讲义必须使用下面的结构。

```md
# 讲义标题

## 1. 本讲目标

说明读者学完后应该掌握什么。

## 2. 前置知识

用通俗语言解释本讲需要的基础概念。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

列出本讲涉及的关键文件，并说明每个文件的作用。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

按最小模块拆分。

每个最小模块都必须包含：

### 4.x 模块名称

#### 4.x.1 概念说明

解释这个模块是什么、解决什么问题、为什么需要它。

#### 4.x.2 核心流程

用列表、流程图式文字或伪代码描述执行过程。

如涉及算法、协议、并发、缓存、调度、状态机等，可以补充必要数学或原理说明。

数学公式使用：

- 行内：\( ... \)
- 独立公式：\[ ... \]

不要使用 `$...$`。

#### 4.x.3 源码精读

引用真实项目代码。

每个关键代码点都要给出永久链接，格式为：

[文件路径:L起始-L结束](<permalink_base>/<相对路径>#L起始-L结束)

链接旁边必须用中文说明这段代码做了什么。

#### 4.x.4 代码实践

给出一个可操作的小实践，例如：

- 运行一个示例。
- 阅读一个测试。
- 修改一个配置。
- 添加一行日志。
- 改一个参数观察行为。
- 编写一个最小调用示例。
- 跟踪一条调用链。

实践步骤要包含：

1. 实践目标。
2. 操作步骤。
3. 需要观察的现象。
4. 预期结果。
5. 如果无法确定运行结果，明确写「待本地验证」。

不要假装已经运行过命令。

#### 4.x.5 小练习与答案

给出 2 到 3 个练习题，并直接给出参考答案。
```

---

## 讲义结尾必须包含

```md
## 5. 综合实践

设计一个贯穿本讲主要内容的小任务，帮助读者把知识串起来。

## 6. 本讲小结

用 3 到 6 条 bullet 总结本讲。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

说明下一讲应该学习什么，或者建议读者继续阅读哪些源码。
```

---

## 代码实践要求

每篇讲义至少包含一个完整代码实践。

实践优先从以下位置寻找依据：

- README
- examples
- tests
- scripts
- package scripts
- Makefile
- CI 配置
- 项目已有 demo

如果找不到可运行示例，也必须提供「源码阅读型实践」，例如：

- 跟踪函数调用链。
- 根据测试断言理解行为。
- 修改局部参数并说明应该观察什么。
- 给关键函数添加日志。
- 阅读配置加载过程并画出流程。

---

## 源码引用要求

- 只引用实际存在的文件。
- 行号必须准确。
- 永久链接必须使用当前 HEAD。
- 如果无法确认行号，不要编造，标注「待确认」。
- 示例代码如果不是项目原有代码，必须明确标注为「示例代码」。

---

## 写作风格

- 中文。
- 深入浅出。
- 先讲直觉，再讲源码。
- 多使用标题、列表、表格和伪代码。
- 不要写空泛总结。
- 不要堆砌大段源码。
- 代码片段要短，只保留关键部分。
- 对初学者不熟悉的术语要解释。

---

## 输出与写入规则

- 只写 stdin 指定的文件。
- 文件路径必须是 `<项目名>-tutorial/<filename>`。
- 不要写其他文件。
- 不要修改源码。
- 完成后，用一句话总结本讲义覆盖了哪些最小模块。

4. 确认本讲义的最小模块。
5. 根据 action 执行：

   - `new`：从零创建该讲义。
   - `rebuild`：从零重建该讲义。
   - `update`：先读取已有讲义，再结合 diff 更新。
   - `keep`：如果被调用，通常不需要编辑文件，只做简短说明。

---

## update 模式规则

当 action 为 `update` 时：

1. 先 `Read` 当前已有的讲义文件。
2. 使用 `git diff previous_head..current_head` 查看相关代码变化。
3. 更新已经失效的源码说明。
4. 刷新所有永久链接中的 head 和行号。
5. 保留仍然正确的内容。
6. 新增必要解释和实践步骤。
7. 如果核心流程已经变化，可以重写受影响章节。

---

## 讲义标准结构

每篇讲义必须使用下面的结构。

```md
# 讲义标题

## 1. 本讲目标

说明读者学完后应该掌握什么。

## 2. 前置知识

用通俗语言解释本讲需要的基础概念。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

列出本讲涉及的关键文件，并说明每个文件的作用。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

按最小模块拆分。

每个最小模块都必须包含：

### 4.x 模块名称

#### 4.x.1 概念说明

解释这个模块是什么、解决什么问题、为什么需要它。

#### 4.x.2 核心流程

用列表、流程图式文字或伪代码描述执行过程。

如涉及算法、协议、并发、缓存、调度、状态机等，可以补充必要数学或原理说明。

数学公式使用：

- 行内：\( ... \)
- 独立公式：\[ ... \]

不要使用 `$...$`。

#### 4.x.3 源码精读

引用真实项目代码。

每个关键代码点都要给出永久链接，格式为：

[文件路径:L起始-L结束](<permalink_base>/<相对路径>#L起始-L结束)

链接旁边必须用中文说明这段代码做了什么。

#### 4.x.4 代码实践

给出一个可操作的小实践，例如：

- 运行一个示例。
- 阅读一个测试。
- 修改一个配置。
- 添加一行日志。
- 改一个参数观察行为。
- 编写一个最小调用示例。
- 跟踪一条调用链。

实践步骤要包含：

1. 实践目标。
2. 操作步骤。
3. 需要观察的现象。
4. 预期结果。
5. 如果无法确定运行结果，明确写「待本地验证」。

不要假装已经运行过命令。

#### 4.x.5 小练习与答案

给出 2 到 3 个练习题，并直接给出参考答案。
```

---

## 讲义结尾必须包含

```md
## 5. 综合实践

设计一个贯穿本讲主要内容的小任务，帮助读者把知识串起来。

## 6. 本讲小结

用 3 到 6 条 bullet 总结本讲。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

说明下一讲应该学习什么，或者建议读者继续阅读哪些源码。
```

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 600000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: ListAgents
tools.description: Lists agents you can SendMessage to — in-process subagents you spawned, the teammates on your team, other local Claude sessions on this machine, your Claude sessions running in the cloud (when this session has cloud access; a cloud session receives your message but cannot message any session back yet — do not ask it to reply, read its answer in its own transcript), and (when Remote Control is connected here) your account's other sessions — Remote Control sessions on other machines and cloud sessions, each row labeled by kind. Names are the address: send with `SendMessage({to: "<name>", message: "..."})`, copying the name exactly as a row prints it. Append a row's ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — two rows share it, or an error asks you to disambiguate.

channel.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

q.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. 63	    def predict_by_feat(self, out, superpoints):
64	        """Predict instance, semantic, and panoptic masks for a single scene.
65	
66	        Args:
67	            out (Dict): Decoder output, each value is List of len 1. Keys:
68	                `cls_preds` of shape (n_queries, n_instance_classes + 1),
69	                `sem_preds` of shape (n_queries, n_semantic_classes + 1),
70	                `masks` of shape (n_queries, n_points),
71	                `scores` of shape (n_queris, 1) or None.
72	            superpoints (Tensor): of shape (n_raw_points,).
73	        
74	        Returns:
75	            List[PointData]: of len 1 with `pts_semantic_mask`,
76	                `pts_instance_mask`, `instance_labels`, `instance_scores`.
77	        """
78	        inst_res = self.predict_by_feat_instance(
79	            out, superpoints, self.test_cfg.inst_score_thr, is_test_iou=self.inst_test_iou)
80	        sem_res = self.predict_by_feat_semantic(out, superpoints)
81	        pan_res = self.predict_by_feat_panoptic(out, superpoints)
82	
83	        pts_semantic_mask = [sem_res.cpu().numpy(), pan_res[0].cpu().numpy()]
84	        pts_instance_mask = [inst_res[0].cpu().bool().numpy(),
85	                             pan_res[1].cpu().numpy()]
86	      
87	        return [
88	            PointData(
89	                pts_semantic_mask=pts_semantic_mask,
90	                pts_instance_mask=pts_instance_mask,
91	                instance_labels=inst_res[1].cpu().numpy(),
92	                instance_scores=inst_res[2].cpu().numpy())]
93	    
94	    def predict_by_feat_instance(self, out, superpoints, score_threshold, is_test_iou=False):
95	        """Predict instance masks for a single scene.
96	
97	        Args:
98	            out (Dict): Decoder output, each value is List of len 1. Keys:
99	                `cls_preds` of shape (n_queries, n_instance_classes + 1),
100	                `masks` of shape (n_queries, n_points),
101	                `scores` of shape (n_queris, 1) or None.
102	            superpoints (Tensor): of shape (n_raw_points,).
103	            score_threshold (float): minimal score for predicted object.
104	        
105	        Returns:
106	            Tuple:
107	                Tensor: mask_preds of shape (n_preds, n_raw_points),
108	                Tensor: labels of shape (n_preds,),
109	                Tensor: scors of shape (n_preds,).
110	        """
111	        cls_preds = out['cls_preds'][0]
112	        pred_masks = out['masks'][0]
113	
114	        scores = F.softmax(cls_preds, dim=-1)[:, :-1]
115	        if out['scores'][0] is not None:
116	            scores *= out['scores'][0]
117	        if is_test_iou:
118	            if out['preds_iou'][0] is not None:
119	                scores *= out['preds_iou'][0]
120	        labels = torch.arange(
121	            self.num_classes,
122	            device=scores.device).unsqueeze(0).repeat(
123	                len(cls_preds), 1).flatten(0, 1)
124	        scores, topk_idx = scores.flatten(0, 1).topk(
125	            self.test_cfg.topk_insts, sorted=False)
126	        labels = labels[topk_idx]
127	    
128	        topk_idx = torch.div(topk_idx, self.num_classes, rounding_mode='floor')
129	        mask_pred = pred_masks
130	        mask_pred = mask_pred[topk_idx]
131	        mask_pred_sigmoid = mask_pred.sigmoid()
132	
133	        if self.test_cfg.get('obj_normalization', None):
134	            mask_scores = (mask_pred_sigmoid * (mask_pred > 0)).sum(1) / \
135	                ((mask_pred > 0).sum(1) + 1e-6)
136	            scores = scores * mask_scores
137	
138	        if self.test_cfg.get('nms', None):
139	            kernel = self.test_cfg.matrix_nms_kernel
140	            scores, labels, mask_pred_sigmoid, _ = mask_matrix_nms(
141	                mask_pred_sigmoid, labels, scores, kernel=kernel)
142	
143	        mask_pred_sigmoid = mask_pred_sigmoid[:, superpoints]
144	        mask_pred = mask_pred_sigmoid > self.test_cfg.sp_score_thr
145	
146	        # score_thr
147	        score_mask = scores > score_threshold
148	        scores = scores[score_mask]
149	        labels = labels[score_mask]
150	        mask_pred = mask_pred[score_mask]
151	
152	        # npoint_thr
153	        mask_pointnum = mask_pred.sum(1)
154	        npoint_mask = mask_pointnum > self.test_cfg.npoint_thr
155	        scores = scores[npoint_mask]
156	        labels = labels[npoint_mask]
157	        mask_pred = mask_pred[npoint_mask]
158	
159	        return mask_pred, labels, scores

161	    def predict_by_feat_semantic(self, out, superpoints, classes=None):

204	
205	        n_stuff_classes = len(self.test_cfg.stuff_classes)
206	        inst_idxs = torch.arange(
207	            n_stuff_classes, 
208	            mask_pred.shape[0] + n_stuff_classes, 
209	            device=mask_pred.device).view(-1, 1)
210	        insts = inst_idxs * mask_pred
211	        things_inst_mask, idxs = insts.max(axis=0)
212	        things_sem_mask = labels[idxs] + n_stuff_classes
213	
214	        inst_idxs, num_pts = things_inst_mask.unique(return_counts=True)
215	        for inst, pts in zip(inst_idxs, num_pts):
216	            if pts <= self.test_cfg.npoint_thr and inst != 0:
217	                things_inst_mask[things_inst_mask == inst] = 0
218	
219	        things_sem_mask[things_inst_mask == 0] = 0
220	      
221	        sem_map[things_inst_mask != 0] = 0
222	        inst_map = sem_map.clone()
223	        inst_map += things_inst_mask
224	        sem_map += things_sem_mask
225	        return sem_map, inst_map

227	    def _select_queries(self, x, gt_instances):
228	        """Select queries for train pass.
229	
230	        Args:
231	            x (List[Tensor]): of len batch_size, each of shape
232	                (n_points_i, n_channels).
233	            gt_instances (List[InstanceData_]): of len batch_size.
234	                Ground truth which can contain `labels` of shape (n_gts_i,),
235	                `sp_masks` of shape (n_gts_i, n_points_i).
236	
237	        Returns:
238	            Tuple:
239	                List[Tensor]: Queries of len batch_size, each queries of shape
240	                    (n_queries_i, n_channels).
241	                List[InstanceData_]: of len batch_size, each updated
242	                    with `query_masks` of shape (n_gts_i, n_queries_i).
243	        """
244	        queries = []
245	        for i in range(len(x)):
246	            if self.query_thr < 1:
247	                n = (1 - self.query_thr) * torch.rand(1) + self.query_thr
248	                n = (n * len(x[i])).int()
249	                n = torch.as_tensor(min(n, 3500)).item()
250	                ids = torch.randperm(len(x[i]))[:n].to(x[i].device)
251	                queries.append(x[i][ids])
252	                gt_instances[i].query_masks = gt_instances[i].sp_masks[:, ids]
253	            else:
254	                queries.append(x[i])
255	                gt_instances[i].query_masks = gt_instances[i].sp_masks
256	            
257	        return queries, gt_instances

362	    def extract_feat(self, x, superpoints, inverse_mapping, batch_offsets):
363	        """Extract features from sparse tensor.
364	
365	        Args:
366	            x (SparseTensor): Input sparse tensor of shape
367	                (n_points, in_channels).
368	            superpoints (Tensor): of shape (n_points,).
369	            inverse_mapping (Tesnor): of shape (n_points,).
370	            batch_offsets (List[int]): of len batch_size + 1.
371	
372	        Returns:
373	            List[Tensor]: of len batch_size,
374	                each of shape (n_points_i, n_channels).
375	        """
376	        x = self.input_conv(x)
377	        x, _ = self.unet(x)
378	        x = self.output_layer(x)
379	        x = scatter_mean(x.features[inverse_mapping], superpoints, dim=0)
380	        out = []
381	        for i in range(len(batch_offsets) - 1):
382	            out.append(x[batch_offsets[i]: batch_offsets[i + 1]])
383	        return out

385	    def collate(self, points, elastic_points=None):
386	        """Collate batch of points to sparse tensor.
387	
388	        Args:
389	            points (List[Tensor]): Batch of points.
390	            quantization_mode (SparseTensorQuantizationMode): Minkowski
391	                quantization mode. We use random sample for training
392	                and unweighted average for inference.
393	
394	        Returns:
395	            TensorField: Containing features and coordinates of a
396	                sparse tensor.
397	        """
398	        if elastic_points is None:
399	            coordinates, features = ME.utils.batch_sparse_collate(
400	                [((p[:, :3] - p[:, :3].min(0)[0]) / self.voxel_size,
401	                  torch.hstack((p[:, 3:], p[:, :3] - p[:, :3].mean(0))))
402	                 for p in points])
403	        else:
404	            coordinates, features = ME.utils.batch_sparse_collate(
405	                [((el_p - el_p.min(0)[0]),
406	                  torch.hstack((p[:, 3:], p[:, :3] - p[:, :3].mean(0))))
407	                 for el_p, p in zip(elastic_points, points)])
408	        
409	        spatial_shape = torch.clip(
410	            coordinates.max(0)[0][1:] + 1, self.min_spatial_shape)
411	        field = ME.TensorField(features=features, coordinates=coordinates)
412	        tensor = field.sparse()
413	        coordinates = tensor.coordinates
414	        features = tensor.features
415	        inverse_mapping = field.inverse_mapping(tensor.coordinate_map_key)
416	
417	        return coordinates, features, inverse_mapping, spatial_shape

423	    def loss(self, batch_inputs_dict, batch_data_samples, **kwargs):
424	        """Calculate losses from a batch of inputs dict and data samples.
425	
426	        Args:
427	            batch_inputs_dict (dict): The model input dict which include
428	                `points` key.
429	            batch_data_samples (List[:obj:`Det3DDataSample`]): The Data
430	                Samples. It includes information such as
431	                `gt_instances_3d` and `gt_sem_seg_3d`.
432	        Returns:
433	            dict: A dictionary of loss components.
434	        """
435	        batch_offsets = [0]
436	        superpoint_bias = 0
437	        sp_gt_instances = []
438	        sp_pts_masks = []
439	        point_prompt_outputs = None
440	        point_prompt_instances = None
441	        text_prompt_outputs = None
442	        text_prompt_instances = None
443	        for i in range(len(batch_data_samples)):
444	            gt_pts_seg = batch_data_samples[i].gt_pts_seg
445	
446	            gt_pts_seg.sp_pts_mask += superpoint_bias
447	            superpoint_bias = gt_pts_seg.sp_pts_mask.max().item() + 1
448	            batch_offsets.append(superpoint_bias)
449	
450	            sp_gt_instances.append(batch_data_samples[i].gt_instances_3d)
451	            sp_pts_masks.append(gt_pts_seg.sp_pts_mask)
452	
453	        coordinates, features, inverse_mapping, spatial_shape = self.collate(
454	            batch_inputs_dict['points'],
455	            batch_inputs_dict.get('elastic_coords', None))
456	
457	        x = spconv.SparseConvTensor(
458	            features, coordinates, spatial_shape, len(batch_data_samples))
459	        sp_pts_masks = torch.hstack(sp_pts_masks)
460	        x = self.extract_feat(
461	            x, sp_pts_masks, inverse_mapping, batch_offsets)
462	        queries, sp_gt_instances = self._select_queries(x, sp_gt_instances)
463	        
464	        if self.set_query_mask:
465	            original_lengths = []
466	            for query in queries:
467	                original_lengths.append(query.shape[0])
468	                
469	        if 'point_prompts' in batch_inputs_dict.keys():
470	            queries, point_prompt_instances = self.add_point_prompt_queries(queries, sp_gt_instances, batch_inputs_dict, x, batch_offsets)
471	        if 'text_token' in batch_inputs_dict.keys():
472	            queries, text_prompt_instances = self.add_text_prompt_queries(queries, sp_gt_instances, batch_inputs_dict, x, batch_offsets)
473	        
474	        if self.set_query_mask:
475	            interaction_masks = []
476	            for m, query in enumerate(queries):
477	                cur_interaction_mask = torch.zeros((query.shape[0], query.shape[0])).bool().to(query.device)
478	                cur_interaction_mask[:original_lengths[m], original_lengths[m]: ] = True
479	                if self.set_all_mask:
480	                    cur_interaction_mask[original_lengths[m]:, :original_lengths[m]] = True
481	                    if query.shape[0] - original_lengths[m] > 0:
482	                        size = query.shape[0] - original_lengths[m]
483	                        inter_mask = torch.eye(size).bool().to(query.device)
484	                        cur_interaction_mask[original_lengths[m]:, original_lengths[m]:] = ~inter_mask
485	                interaction_masks.append(cur_interaction_mask)
486	                pass
487	        else:
488	            interaction_masks = None    
489	            
490	        # Compute superpoint centroids (positions) per sample for position-aware aggregation
491	        raw_positions = torch.vstack([p[:, :3] for p in batch_inputs_dict['points']]).to(sp_pts_masks.device)
492	        sp_centroids = scatter_mean(raw_positions, sp_pts_masks, dim=0)
493	        point_positions = [sp_centroids[batch_offsets[i]: batch_offsets[i + 1]] for i in range(len(batch_offsets) - 1)]
494	
495	        x = self.decoder(x, queries, interaction_masks=interaction_masks, point_positions=point_positions)
496	        
497	        if 'text_token' in batch_inputs_dict.keys():
498	            x, text_prompt_outputs = self.split_original_and_text_prompt_queries(x, batch_inputs_dict)
499	        if 'point_prompts' in batch_inputs_dict.keys():
500	            x, point_prompt_outputs = self.split_original_and_point_prompt_queries(x, batch_inputs_dict)
501	
502	        if self.pred_iou:
503	            x = self.get_pred_iou(x)
504	
505	        loss = self.criterion(x, sp_gt_instances, point_prompt_outputs, point_prompt_instances, text_prompt_outputs, text_prompt_instances)
506	        return loss

1028	    def collate(self, points, elastic_points=None):
1029	        """Collate batch of points to sparse tensor.
1030	
1031	        Args:
1032	            points (List[Tensor]): Batch of points.
1033	            quantization_mode (SparseTensorQuantizationMode): Minkowski
1034	                quantization mode. We use random sample for training

1039	                sparse tensor.

1041	        if elastic_points is None:
1042	            coordinates, features = ME.utils.batch_sparse_collate(
1043	                [((p[:, :3] - p[:, :3].min(0)[0]) / self.voxel_size,
1044	                  torch.hstack((p[:, 3:], p[:, :3] - p[:, :3].mean(0))))
1045	                 for p in points])
1046	        else:
1047	            coordinates, features = ME.utils.batch_sparse_collate(
1048	                [((el_p - el_p.min(0)[0]),
1049	                  torch.hstack((p[:, 3:], p[:, :3] - p[:, :3].mean(0))))
1050	                 for el_p, p in zip(elastic_points, points)])
1051	        
1052	        spatial_shape = torch.clip(
1053	            coordinates.max(0)[0][1:] + 1, self.min_spatial_shape)

1055	        tensor = field.sparse()

1057	        features = tensor.features
1058	        inverse_mapping = field.inverse_mapping(tensor.coordinate_map_key)
1059	
1060	        return coordinates, features, inverse_mapping, spatial_shape

1481	    def collate(self, points, elastic_points=None):
1482	        """Collate batch of points to sparse tensor.
1483	
1484	        Args:
1485	            points (List[Tensor]): Batch of points.
1486	            quantization_mode (SparseTensorQuantizationMode): Minkowski
1487	                quantization mode. We use random sample for training

1491	            TensorField: Containing features and coordinates of a
1492	                sparse tensor.
1493	        """
1494	        if elastic_points is None:
1495	            coordinates, features = ME.utils.batch_sparse_collate(
1496	                [((p[:, :3] - p[:, :3].min(0)[0]) / self.voxel_size,
1497	                  torch.hstack((p[:, 3:], p[:, :3] - p[:, :3].mean(0))))
1498	                 for p in points])
1499	        else:
1500	            coordinates, features = ME.utils.batch_sparse_collate(
1501	                [((el_p - el_p.min(0)[0]),
1502	                  torch.hstack((p[:, 3:], p[:, :3] - p[:, :3].mean(0))))
1503	                 for el_p, p in zip(elastic_points, points)])
1504	        
1505	        spatial_shape = torch.clip(
1506	            coordinates.max(0)[0][1:] + 1, self.min_spatial_shape)
1507	        field = ME.TensorField(features=features, coordinates=coordinates)
1508	        tensor = field.sparse()
1509	        coordinates = tensor.coordinates
1510	        features = tensor.features
1511	        inverse_mapping = field.inverse_mapping(tensor.coordinate_map_key)
1512	
1513	        return coordinates, features, inverse_mapping, spatial_shape

1857	        """Predict results from a batch of inputs and data samples with post-
1858	        processing.
1859	
1860	        Args:
1861	            batch_inputs_dict (dict): The model input dict which include
1862	                `points` key.

1874	                - pts_instance_mask (Tensor): Instance mask, has a shape

1877	        batch_offsets = [0]
1878	        superpoint_bias = 0
1879	        sp_pts_masks = []
1880	        sp_gt_instances = []
1881	        for i in range(len(batch_data_samples)):
1882	            gt_pts_seg = batch_data_samples[i].gt_pts_seg
1883	            gt_pts_seg.sp_pts_mask += superpoint_bias
1884	            superpoint_bias = gt_pts_seg.sp_pts_mask.max().item() + 1

1891	            batch_inputs_dict['points'])
1892

1894	            features, coordinates, spatial_shape, len(batch_data_samples))
1895	        sp_pts_masks = torch.hstack(sp_pts_masks)
1896	        x = self.extract_feat(
1897	            x, sp_pts_masks, inverse_mapping, batch_offsets)
1898	        
1899	        queries = copy.deepcopy(x)
1900	        
1901	        if self.set_query_mask:
1902	            original_lengths = []

1904	                original_lengths.append(query.shape[0])
1905

1910

1915	                cur_interaction_mask[:original_lengths[m], original_lengths[m]: ] = True

1918	                    if query.shape[0] - original_lengths[m] > 0:
